title: Characterization of the halting function
statement: Let $c$ be a machine representation scheme and let $s$ be a bit string. The halting function of $c$ returns true on $s$ if and only if there are bit strings $\alpha$ and $x$ such that $s$ is their pairing encoding, and the machine decoded from $\alpha$ produces some output on input $x$ within some finite number of steps.
replaced:
Let $c$ be a coding scheme for Turing machines and let $s$ be a bit string. Then
$\mathrm{HALT}_c(s)$ is true if and only if there exist bit strings $\alpha$ and
$x$ such that $s$ is the pairing encoding $\langle \alpha, x \rangle$ and the
machine that $\alpha$ denotes under $c$ produces some output on input $x$ within
some finite number of steps.
